subject: general
question: The population of a village was 2,90,000. It increased by 10% in the first year and increased by 30% in the second year. Its population after two years is _______.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive Multiplier for 10% and 30% increase = 1.1 × 1.3 = 1.43

Initial Population = 2,90,000

Population after 2 years = 2,90,000 × 1.43

Population after 2 years = 4,14,700

**∴ Answer = 4,14,700**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Population = 2,90,000

Increase in 1st year = 10%

Increase in 2nd year = 30%

**Formula used:**

Final Population = Initial Population × (1 + r₁/100) × (1 + r₂/100)

 
• 2,90,000 Initial 
 +10% 3,19,000 Year 1 
 +30% 4,14,700 Year 2 
 

**Calculations:**

Population after the 1st year = 2,90,000 × (110 ÷ 100)

⇒ 2,90,000 × 1.1 = 3,19,000

Population after the 2nd year = 3,19,000 × (130 ÷ 100)

⇒ 3,19,000 × 1.3 = 4,14,700

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Formula

For two successive changes of a% and b%, the net effective change is (a + b + (a × b ÷ 100))%.

Population Depreciation

If the population decreases by r% every year, the population after n years is P × (1 − r ÷ 100)ⁿ.

Effective Growth Rate

The single equivalent growth rate for 10% and 30% is 10 + 30 + (10 × 30 ÷ 100) = 43%.
